subject.title: [Bug]: clearUnboundScopes strips operator scopes unconditionally for non-local token-auth clients

question: Should device-less non-local shared-token/password WebSocket operator clients receive operator scopes, and if so should those scopes come from bounded configuration/device trust rather than client-declared scopes?
rationale: Current source and docs intentionally clear self-declared scopes for this class of client, while the reported fix would grant operator.write or stronger permissions across a network auth boundary.

options.title: Land bounded token policy
options.body: Use a reviewed tokenScopes or device-bound policy that grants only configured scopes and keeps exposed Gateway deployments fail-closed by default.

options.title: Restore self-declared scopes
options.body: Allow valid shared-token clients to retain requested scopes, accepting the broader trust model for anyone with the shared token.

options.title: Keep current clearing default
options.body: Document the current device-identity requirement and route headless deployments to pairing/device-token or future config work.

recommendation.title: Land bounded token policy
recommendation.body: Use a reviewed tokenScopes or device-bound policy that grants only configured scopes and keeps exposed Gateway deployments fail-closed by default.

likelyOwner.reason: The open tokenScopes implementation candidate and related config/security discussion are tied to this account in current history.
